'''''Fissidens''''' is the only genus of [[Peristome#In mosses|haplolepideous]] [[moss]]es ([[Dicranidae]]) in the family [[Fissidentaceae]].<ref name=bryonames/> It contains over 480 species.

==Morphology==
''Fissidens'' is an [[acrocarpous]] genus characterized by the presence of vaginal lamina on their leaves, which may be palmately or pinnately arranged.  Each leaf consists of one dorsal lamina, which is the farthest away from the central strand, and two vaginal lamina which clasp the central strand.  They are connected via a single costa, though this costa is infrequently nearly absent.<ref name="WFO">{{cite web |title=Fissidens Hedw. |url=https://www.worldfloraonline.org/taxon/wfo-4000014805 |website=World Flora Online |access-date=24 February 2026}}</ref>

==Subordinate taxa==
''Fissidens'' is generally accepted to include multiple subgenera, though these are disputed from publication to publication.  A 2004 publication on the infrageneric taxonomy included four: ''Aloma,'' ''Fissidens'', ''Octodiceras'', and ''Pachyfissidens''.<ref name="Pursell2004">{{cite journal |last1=Pursell |first1=Ronald |last2=Bruggeman-Nannenga |first2=Maria |title=A Revision of the Infrageneric Taxa of Fissidens |journal=The Bryologist |date=Spring 2004 |volume=107 |issue=1 |pages=1-20 |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/3244563 |access-date=24 February 2026}}</ref> In 2018, the clade ''Fissidens'' was confirmed to be [[monophyletic]] and only three subgenera were recognized: ''Fissidens,'' ''Pachyfissidens,'' and the novel ''Neoamblyothallia''.<ref name="YMPEV 6171">{{cite journal |last1=Suzuki |first1=Tadashi |last2=Inoue |first2=Yuya |last3=Tsubota |first3=Hiromi |title=Molecular phylogeny of the genus Fissidens (Fissidentaceae, Bryophyta) and a refinement of the infrageneric classification |journal=Molecular Phylogenetics and Evolution |date=May 2018 |volume=127 |pages=190-202 |doi=10.1016/j.ympev.2018.05.020}}</ref>

Subsequent analysis of these clades found that the subgenera ''Aloma'' and ''Octodiceras'' as described by Pursell and Bruggeman-Nannenga in 2004, were strongly indicated to be monophyletic.  Three sections described in 2018 were also indicated to be monophyletic, but none of the subgenera were.{{efn|name="monophyletic sections"|The monophyletic sections are ''Neoamblyothallia'' sect. ''Neoamblyothallia'', ''Pachyfissidens'' sect. ''Pachyfissidens'', and ''Fissidens'' sect. ''Aerofissidens''.}} This 2022 infrageneric analysis determined that all other subgenera and sections were nonmonophyletic.<ref name="Budke2022">{{cite journal |last1=Budke |first1=Jessica |last2=Patel |first2=Nikisha |last3=GoFlag Consortium |last4=Wienhold |first4=Mark |last5=Bruggeman-Nannenga |first5=Maria |title=Exploring morphological evolution in relation to habitat moisture in the moss genus Fissidens using molecular data generated from herbarium specimens |journal=Journal of Systematics and Evolution |date=October 2022 |volume=61 |issue=5 |pages=868-889 |doi=10.1111/jse.12926 |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/365021554_Exploring_morphological_evolution_in_relation_to_habitat_moisture_in_the_moss_genus_Fissidens_using_molecular_data_generated_from_herbarium_specimens |access-date=24 February 2026}}</ref>
